items.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Eddie Tompkins. I replaced Eddie Tompkins.

ctx.x: Eddie Tompkins. I replaced Eddie Tompkins. Well then I think that’s when I started really concentrating on playing lead trumpet. And so from then on I turned out to be a lead trumpet player. And so I kind of forgot being a Louis or a Roy or some of them other people, and I started concentrating on being a lead trumpet player.
Yeah. But you got your licks in later on. I’ve got the records to prove that.

items.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Eddie Tompkins walked off of the stage in Washington, DC from the band and they never knew why he left

ctx.x: Why did you come into the band? Why did Eddie Tompkins leave?

Eddie Tompkins, that‘s a good question. That is a very good question. Eddie Tompkins walked off of the stage in Washington, DC from the band and they never knew why he left and he never came back. He walked off of the stage in Washington, DC and Gerald Wilson said, ―I‘ve got a trumpet player who could come and play, replace Eddie Tompkins.‖ Gerald told him about me and Jimmie Lunceford went to school with a funeral man in Dayton that had a funeral parlor and everything; used to tell Jimmie about me. And so that…

When you say it was tough, was it because the other musicians they didn‘t treat you well? Or was it that the work was so rigorous or demanding? Why did you say it was tough working with Jimmie Lunceford?
